drhp.business: The Company provides operation, maintenance and field-level execution of works relating to electricity distribution networks and associated infrastructure, including distribution lines, feeders, substations, poles and cables. Operations are organised into three service verticals: Network O&M Services, Electrical Infrastructure and Network Development Works, and Metering and Meter Management Services. Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tenders by electricity distribution utilities under rate contracts, outline agreements or annual maintenance contracts, with work orders issued …

It also intends to expand its geographical presence into additional states and regions - currently Odisha accounts for 69.05% of Fiscal 2026 …
drhp.one_liner: Incorporated in 1985, a power distribution infrastructure services provider offering operation and maintenance (O&M) and allied support services primarily to electricity distribution utilities in India.

Electrical Infrastructure and Network De: Pole-related works including erection and shifting of poles
Cable-related works including laying, jointing and termination of underground and overhead cables
Civil works such as excavation, foundation works, construction of plinths and other supporting civil structures
Metering and Meter Management Services: Installation and replacement of energy meters
Network Operation and Maintenance (O&M): Maintenance and operational support of electrical distribution systems across 33 kV, 11 kV and low-tension (LT) networks
Deployment of technical manpower for line maintenance, network inspection and fault rectification
System monitoring, fault detection, troubleshooting and repair of distribution networks and substations
Installation, testing and commissioning of distribution systems across 33 kV, 11 kV, HT and LT networks

risks.note: A major portion of revenue is derived from electricity distribution utilities (79.10% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, 88.73% in Fiscal 2025, 88.87% in Fiscal 2024); any reduction in business from such customers, adverse changes in procurement practices or failure to secure new contracts may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows
risks.risk: Customer-segment concentration on power distribution utilities

risks.note: Demand for the Company's services is directly linked to the level of investment in electricity distribution infrastructure, which is influenced by capital expenditure programmes of utilities, availability of funding, government policies and reforms, and implementation of sectoral schemes such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme
risks.risk: Dependence on sector capital expenditure, government policy and schemes such as RDSS

risks.note: Electricity distribution utilities operate within a regulated framework and are subject to approval processes and performance requirements prescribed by regulatory authorities; their financial position and investment capacity affect the Company
risks.risk: Regulated counterparties with constrained financial position and investment capacity

risks.note: Realization of revenues from the order book of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores is subject to commencement and progress of projects, issuance of work orders, site availability, customer approvals and other factors beyond the Company's control; there can be no assurance the entire order book will convert into revenue within expected timelines or at all
Odisha contributed 69.05%, 74.52% and 67.09% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively, leaving revenue exposed to a single state's distribution capex and tendering

risks.risk: Dependence on competitive tendering and repeat orders

Any failure to secure contracts through competitive tendering processes, inability to meet eligibility requirements, or sustained pressure on pricing or margins may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.
Any delay or default in payments may adversely impact our liquidity and increase our working capital requirements.

internal_operational.risk: A major portion of our revenue is derived from power distribution utilities, and any reduction in business from such customers, adverse changes in procurement practices or failure to secure new contracts may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

Any reduction or delay in capital expenditure, regulatory framework or sectoral priorities, or any constraints affecting the investment capacity of electricity distribution utilities, may reduce the demand for our services.
Further, any shift in customer focus towards capital expenditure-

Our ability to secure contracts depends on our ability to meet the eligibility requirements specified in tender documents, including criteria relating to prior experience, financial capacity, technical qualifications, availability of manpower and statutory registrations.

A significant portion of our revenue from operations is derived from a limited number of customers, and any reduction in business from such customers may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

strategy_growth.risk: The execution of our projects and service contracts depends on our ability to mobilize and deploy adequate manpower across geographies, including key operational locations such as Odisha, Delhi, Mumbai, Gujarat and Ajmer.

Given the project-based and geographically dispersed nature of our operations, we establish offices, storage facilities and residential accommodations for personnel at or near project locations, which are generally taken on short-term rental or license basis depending on project requirements.

A significant portion of our revenue from operations is concentrated in certain geographical regions, and any adverse developments affecting such regions may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows

34 A significant portion of our revenue from operations is derived from projects and service assignments executed in certain geographical regions of India, particularly in Odisha and Maharashtra, along with presence in other states.

Our geographical concentration exposes us to risks associated with adverse developments in such regions, including changes in state government policies, delays in infrastructure spending by electricity distribution utilities, regulatory changes, labour disruptions, social or civil unrest, adverse economic conditions, extreme weather events, natural disasters or other regional factors beyond our control.

Our operations are spread across multiple project locations, and any inability to effectively manage and coordinate such geographically dispersed operations may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- A major portion of revenue is derived from electricity distribution utilities (79.10% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026, 88.73% in Fiscal 2025, 88.87% in Fiscal 2024); any reduction in business from such customers, adverse changes in procurement practices or failure to secure new contracts may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and cash flows
- Demand for the Company's services is directly linked to the level of investment in electricity distribution infrastructure, which is influenced by capital expenditure programmes of utilities, availability of funding, government policies and reforms, and implementation of sectoral schemes such as the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme
- Electricity distribution utilities operate within a regulated framework and are subject to approval processes and performance requirements prescribed by regulatory authorities; their financial position and investment capacity affect the Company
- Realization of revenues from the order book of approximately Rs. 553.70 crores is subject to commencement and progress of projects, issuance of work orders, site availability, customer approvals and other factors beyond the Company's control; there can be no assurance the entire order book will convert into revenue within expected timelines or at all
- Odisha contributed 69.05%, 74.52% and 67.09% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively, leaving revenue exposed to a single state's distribution capex and tendering
- Contracts are typically awarded through competitive tender processes; ability to continue receiving repeat orders depends on performance of existing contracts, customer requirements, competitive bidding and other external factors, and repeat-customer revenue share has declined from 99.28% (FY 2023-24) to 88.29% (FY 2025-26)
- Execution depends on deployment of a 4,473-person workforce (as of May 31, 2026) of supervisors, linemen, technicians and helpers across designated service areas, supported by vehicles, tools and equipment, with defined operating procedures required for high-voltage work
